summary: Run this one first, as the single stage-2 check. Fold in the diagnostic half of s2-per-kernel-enable: judge w13+silu and w2 independently, and do not abort on the first non-finite value. Also add prepare-time per-kernel timing against Marlin and a compact summary printed last. One check then names the faulty kernel and tensor, and gives M2 evidence for both kernels even if correctness still fails. Hold the two siblings on this result.
justification: Design (kind: rewrite): unchanged from stage 1b and still sound. At bs=128 and 256, Marlin is 292.5 and 391.4 us, 95% of each shape (FINDINGS), against floors of 101.3 and 108.9 us. A swap-AB wgmma with register-A dequant and TMA-fed token slabs is the right tensor-core path there. Stage 1b proved the build (sm_90a only, 32.8 s), the TMA maps (rc 0) and every launch (error word 0). The remaining problem is numerical. Reading stage 1b's code (branch hyp/muse_moe_w4a16/cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-sm90a-rebuild-inproc) narrows the suspects. (a) The E2M1/E4M3 dequant bit trick, the code/scale retiling order and the A-fragment register order are verbatim from the swap-AB sibling, which passed rel-L2 9.2e-3 on the judge. They are unlikely to cause the bug, though wgmma RS should still be checked to confirm it uses the same per-warp A layout as mma.sync m16k16 (rows 16w..16w+15). (b) The B descriptor (start>>4, LBO 1, SBO 1024, layout type 1 = 128B swizzle, +32 B per k16, 1024-aligned boxes) and expect_tx = 9216 + 2*(16<<b)*128 look right on paper and are exactly what the numpy emulation must confirm. (c) The canary checks only `out`, and cache3 is torch.empty. Any local route whose w2 row is never written (a chunk-coverage or epilogue-scatter bug) is uninitialised caching-allocator memory, which is a very common non-finite source and needs no wrong math at all. wg_hs is torch.zeros, so an unwritten h row shows up as a wrong value rather than a NaN. The canary covers only bucket N=128 with one 8-block chunk: N=16/32/64 and multi-chunk experts have never run. WEAKEST LINK: the spec's fix (2), zeroing the smem ring and the cache2/y rows, can turn a NaN into a finite wrong answer. It masks an expect_tx-short race or an unwritten row instead of fixing it. Finiteness is therefore not the pass criterion: canary and self-check must gate on rel-L2 against Marlin per kernel. Use a SENTINEL fill, not zeros, in the diagnostic pass so 'never written' and 'computed non-finite' can be told apart. SECOND: wgmma_wait<1> keeps one group in flight while the next iteration's dequant rewrites the A registers. That is undefined behaviour for RS wgmma unless ptxas serialises it. ptxas normally does serialise it, with the warning 'wgmma.mma_async instructions are serialized due to non wgmma instructions defining input registers'. The result is correct but slow, so it is an M2 risk rather than a NaN suspect. The build stderr is never shown (the archived log is a ~15 KB tail), so capture it and print a one-line summary of any 'serialized' warning late. Expected directions (bs>=128 faster, bs<128 flat controls) are consistent with TASK.md weights and floors.
confounders: align-parallel-per-expert-verify (master): at bs>=128 the wgmma path bypasses _align_parallel_kernel (4.0/6.9 us) for expert_map gather + moe_align_block_size(16) + wg_gather. Add that delta to the replaced-kernel sum. It is small against ~300-400 us and does not confound M1/M2.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: these set the incumbent Marlin rows (block_size_m 16 at bs=128, 32 at bs=256). Compare against this run's own fallback-free master profile. Marlin row noise between identical-code runs is +/-10-20% (275.0 vs 292.5 us at bs=128, 425.4 vs 391.4 us at bs=256).

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no interaction at bs>=128, because both paths use SGLang's fused norm with slot_expert_ids. It does matter for (1d): the Triton kernel's docstring says remote y rows are uninitialised and skipped, and the fused SGLang kernel is assumed to skip them as well. Verify this rather than assume it.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: defines the Marlin bank used as the reference in the canary and self-check. A shared quantisation-convention error (global-scale direction) would cancel against Marlin, but the existing fp32-dequant expert check covers that.
interference: No ab-revert or ab-tune companion is needed: it is a rewrite, and the fallback keeps master's path, so the landed hypotheses cannot fake a gain. The real interference is between the three stage-2 siblings, which all depend on the same unfixed bug. Running them in parallel spends three checks to learn one fact. Merge the diagnostic part of s2-per-kernel-enable into this run. Do NOT merge its mixed Marlin/wgmma production path: that needs a bridge, and Marlin's block_size_m (16/32) differs from the wgmma align block 16, so it is a stage-3 item only if exactly one kernel passes. Hold s2-fix-gate-from-8 until this run gives M1/M2 at >=128. Required design so the single check pinpoints the fault: (A) never raise on the first non-finite value. Run the canary as a diagnostic that always completes, then fall back. (B) Pre-fill wg_hs, wg_xs pad rows and cache3 with a distinctive finite sentinel (e.g. bf16 -12345.0) for the diagnostic pass only, and report per tensor: rows unwritten (still sentinel), rows non-finite, first bad (row, col, col//BN, tile j, chunk, bucket) and rel-L2 on finite rows. (C) Judge w13+silu (h at sorted slots mapped back to routes, against Marlin w13 + silu_and_mul) and w2 (fed Marlin's cache2 gathered into h_sorted by the existing gather logic with sid instead of sid>>3, against Marlin w2) independently. Do this at the canary M=128 AND at a multi-bucket case: M=256 skewed hits buckets 16/32/64 and multi-chunk experts. (D) If launches stay fault-free, run the full self-check in diagnostic mode even when the canary fails numerically. It has already been shown not to fault, and its per-case h/y/out rel-L2 is the localisation. Cut its graph before/after replay lines to one line per case so the tail is not flooded. (E) Time each wgmma kernel against its Marlin counterpart in prepare at M=128 and 256, using CUDA events and the median of 20. A NaN does not change speed, so M2 evidence arrives even if M1 fails. Discount by the 20-25% prepare undercount noted in LESSONS and treat the number as optimistic if the bug is an early-release race. (F) Print one compact block LAST in prepare: build flags, regs/spill, ptxas 'serialized' yes/no, per-kernel verdict (unwritten/non-finite/rel-L2), per-kernel prepare us vs Marlin, and PATH CHOSEN. The archived log keeps only the last ~15 KB. Do the numpy emulation in (3) before dispatch, as the spec says. If it finds a definite mismatch, fix it and still keep A-F.
rules_flags: None blocking. Smem zeroing, sentinel fills and per-kernel timing are all in prepare() or inside the kernel. Nothing is derived from timed inputs and there is no host sync in kernel_fn.
Keep sentinel fills to the prepare-time diagnostic pass. In kernel_fn, any extra zero_() of cache3 is a timed launch and must be counted in the replaced-kernel sum.
Keep the path decision a prepare-time correctness flag. Do not choose the path from prepare timing in this stage (print only).
open_questions: Does SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum with slot_expert_ids skip slots with local id -1? Read its source offline before the check. If it does, (1d) is moot and the canary's 7 remote routes are harmless.

Does ptxas serialise the wgmma pipeline (A registers rewritten while one group is in flight)? If it does, M2 needs double-buffered A fragments, or wait<0> before the dequant of stage n+1 overlaps differently. That is the stage-3 performance fix.
FINDINGS line 66 says stage 1b 'gained on verify_16; verify_32'. That is wrong: it was a Marlin rerun, and it should be corrected so later hypothesis minting does not cite it.
Prepare budget: build 32.8 s, plus diagnostic canary, full self-check (20-60 s) and per-kernel timing. Keep WG_SETUP_BUDGET_S and log the total seconds.
